domain_symbols.analytic_space: domains, function spaces, and analytic structures
domain_symbols.operator_space: operators and transforms on function spaces

rules.name: Holomorphicity in several variables seed
rules.input_form: function on C^n
preconditions: A domain in C^n and complex-variable structure are fixed
rules.operation: Recognize holomorphicity in the several-complex-variables setting.
examples: Several-complex-variable holomorphicity is stricter than separately checking arbitrary real differentiability conditions
counterexamples: Continuity alone on C^n is insufficient for holomorphicity

rules.name: PDE classification seed
rules.input_form: second-order linear PDE principal part
preconditions: The principal second-order coefficients are fixed
rules.operation: Classify a second-order linear PDE by its principal-part quadratic form.
examples: Heat, Laplace, and wave equations fall into distinct PDE classes under principal-symbol analysis
counterexamples: Classifying a PDE by lower-order terms alone is invalid

rules.name: Dynamical system orbit seed
rules.input_form: initial state and evolution rule
preconditions: A time evolution map or flow is fixed
rules.operation: Generate the orbit of an initial state under repeated or continuous evolution.
examples: Long-term behavior questions in dynamics are phrased in terms of orbits, invariant sets, and recurrence
counterexamples: Treating one isolated time step as a full orbit is invalid

rules.name: Fourier transform seed
rules.input_form: integrable or transformable function
preconditions: A standard Fourier-transform convention is fixed
rules.operation: Convert a function into its frequency-domain transform.
examples: Oscillatory structure becomes algebraic frequency data under Fourier transformation
counterexamples: Replacing the transform by pointwise multiplication is invalid

rules.name: Banach space completeness seed
rules.input_form: normed vector space
preconditions: A norm and induced metric are fixed
rules.operation: Recognize a Banach space by norm completeness.
examples: Completeness permits limit arguments for Cauchy sequences of functions or vectors in the active norm
counterexamples: A normed space need not be Banach if Cauchy sequences fail to converge inside the space

rules.name: Bounded linear operator seed
rules.input_form: linear map between normed spaces
preconditions: Domain and codomain normed spaces are fixed
rules.operation: Equate boundedness and continuity for linear maps in normed spaces.
examples: Operator norm control gives continuity of linear maps between normed spaces
counterexamples: Nonlinear continuity does not define a bounded linear operator

rules.name: Fredholm integral equation seed
rules.input_form: unknown function under integral operator with fixed kernel
preconditions: A kernel, domain of integration, and function space are fixed
rules.operation: Represent an equation as a Fredholm integral equation on a function space.
examples: Integral equations can be rewritten as operator equations on function spaces
counterexamples: Treating arbitrary pointwise equations as integral equations is invalid

rules.name: Montel normal family seed
rules.input_form: locally bounded family of holomorphic functions
preconditions: A standard several-complex-variables domain and local boundedness assumptions are fixed
rules.operation: Use Montel-type compactness for locally bounded holomorphic families.
examples: Compactness of function families in several complex variables is controlled by holomorphic boundedness rather than by arbitrary pointwise behavior alone
counterexamples: An unconstrained family of holomorphic functions is not automatically normal

rules.name: Sobolev weak derivative seed
rules.category: partial differential equations and functional analysis
rules.input_form: function with weak derivative structure and integrability data
preconditions: A domain, integrability exponent, and weak derivative interpretation are fixed
rules.operation: Treat weak differentiability and integrability jointly through Sobolev-space structure.
examples: PDE solutions can be treated variationally even when classical derivatives fail to exist everywhere
counterexamples: Demanding pointwise smoothness everywhere is invalid as a general Sobolev criterion

rules.name: Semigroup evolution seed
rules.category: partial differential equations and dynamical systems
rules.input_form: operator-generated time-evolution family
preconditions: A linear evolution generator and semigroup law are fixed
rules.operation: Model time evolution through operator semigroups.
examples: Time propagation for heat-type problems is organized by semigroup structure rather than by isolated time steps only
counterexamples: Arbitrary families of operators with no semigroup law do not define semigroup evolution

rules.name: Attractor invariance seed
rules.input_form: dynamical system with candidate long-term invariant set
preconditions: An invariant-set framework and asymptotic notion are fixed
rules.operation: Summarize long-term behavior through invariant attracting sets.
examples: Asymptotic dynamics are summarized by invariant sets rather than by one transient orbit segment
counterexamples: Any bounded set visited once is not automatically an attractor

rules.name: Plancherel seed
rules.input_form: square-integrable function under a Fourier-transform convention
preconditions: An L2 setting and transform normalization are fixed
rules.operation: Preserve quadratic energy under Fourier transformation up to normalization convention.
examples: Frequency-domain analysis can conserve quadratic energy even while changing representation completely
counterexamples: Assuming arbitrary transforms preserve L2 norm without the required theorem is invalid

rules.name: Compact operator seed
rules.input_form: bounded operator on a normed or Banach setting
preconditions: A bounded-set and relative-compactness interpretation are fixed
rules.operation: Recognize compact operators by relative compactness of images of bounded sets.
examples: Compactness gives spectral discreteness features absent for generic bounded operators
counterexamples: Boundedness alone does not imply compactness

rules.name: Spectral theorem seed
rules.input_form: self-adjoint or normal operator with spectral setting
preconditions: A spectral setting for self-adjoint or normal operators is fixed
rules.operation: Decompose suitable operators through spectral data.
examples: Diagonalization ideas extend from finite matrices to operators through spectral measures or analogous decompositions
counterexamples: Arbitrary nonnormal operators do not automatically satisfy the standard spectral theorem

rules.name: Green function seed
rules.category: partial differential equations and integral equations
rules.input_form: linear operator with boundary-value problem
preconditions: A linear differential operator and boundary conditions are fixed
rules.operation: Represent forced solutions through Green-function kernels.
examples: Forcing-response structure can be encoded by kernels rather than solved from scratch for every right-hand side
counterexamples: Ignoring boundary conditions while claiming a Green-function solution is invalid

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
rules.input_form: raw expression E
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rewrite expressions into a canonical form that preserves the active equivalence relation.
examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings
counterexamples: Applying canonicalization rules outside their preconditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Substitution soundness expansion
rules.input_form: expression F(x) with admissible substitution x <- g
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Substitute only under explicit domain and structural admissibility constraints.
examples: Replacing a variable by a constrained expression must preserve declared domain assumptions
counterexamples: Substitution that violates assumptions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Composition rule expansion
rules.input_form: objects A and B with a valid composition law
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Compose structured objects when composition preconditions are satisfied.
examples: Function and operator compositions require compatible codomain-domain interfaces
counterexamples: Composing incompatible objects is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Inverse admissibility expansion
rules.input_form: object A with invertibility conditions
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Introduce inverses only when invertibility conditions are explicitly satisfied.
examples: Matrix inversion requires nonsingularity
counterexamples: Assuming inverses exist without conditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Constraint propagation expansion
rules.input_form: state with constraints C and transform T
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Propagate constraints through each accepted transformation step.
examples: Positivity or boundedness constraints should be preserved or updated after transformation
counterexamples: Dropping constraints silently is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Boundary condition integration expansion
rules.input_form: model equation with boundary or endpoint constraints
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Include boundary and endpoint constraints in the active model state before solving.
examples: Differential models require boundary or initial data to identify admissible solution families
counterexamples: Solving while ignoring required boundary conditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Conservation tracking expansion
rules.input_form: model evolution with candidate conserved quantity Q
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Track whether declared conserved quantities remain invariant under model evolution.
examples: Energy-like quantities can be validated as conserved under symmetry assumptions
counterexamples: Declaring conservation without validation is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Approximation error budget expansion
rules.input_form: approximation method and tolerance epsilon
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Attach explicit error bounds or estimates to approximation-driven outputs.
examples: Numerical approximations should report residual or tolerance-constrained error
counterexamples: Reporting approximations without any error control is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Parameter sensitivity expansion
rules.input_form: model output O(theta) with parameter vector theta
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Quantify how parameter perturbations affect outputs and derived conclusions.
examples: Small parameter shifts can cause large output changes near bifurcation or instability regions
counterexamples: Assuming robustness with no sensitivity analysis is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Symmetry detection expansion
rules.input_form: equation or model M
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Detect and record symmetry transformations that preserve model structure.
examples: Translation or rotation symmetries can simplify derivations and reduce state dimensionality
counterexamples: Attributing symmetry to a model that breaks it under constraints is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions
